facts.text: Milton was settled in 1760 as part of Rochester, originally called 'Three Ponds' before becoming its own town.
The first saw‑mill in Milton, built by Samuel Palmer in 1775 at Three Ponds, sits near the present dam.
The town’s distinctive 1808 Milton Town House and the 1875 Milton Free Public Library, a former schoolhouse, showcase its historic architecture.
Milton Mills was the terminus of the Great Falls and Conway railroad, linking the town to the North Conway division of the Eastern Railroad in the 19th century.
The Milton Historical Society, housed in a 1916 building that once served as a library, preserves and shares the town’s heritage through collections and education.
In 1844 a cotton factory was built at Three Ponds, but it burned in September 1845 after only a few months of operation.
